source.original_title: 07/02/2026 - Michael Mazey x Andrew Musial KFS
source.display_title: 07/02/2026 - Michael Mazey x Andrew Musial KFS — Follow Up

rep.name: Michael Brideau
rep.location: Colombia (travelling; operates on US Central time)

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I went through everything that you and Kim chatted about already, plus your application'; prospect: 'the whole concept that I was talking about with Kim on the phone'

prospect.name: Michael Mazey
prospect.family_status: Single; recently ended a pursuit of one woman who ghosted him; describes dating as an original driver
prospect.training_background: Cross-country distance runner in high school (~50 miles/week); gym/machine and free-weight phases in college that did not stick; currently table tennis ~5x/week, rec volleyball weekly, basketball 1-2x/week, hiking every 2-3 weekends; walked 10-15k steps/day for Nov-early Dec then it lapsed; has experimented with calisthenics, dumbbells and barbells
prospect.medical: Diagnosed hypothyroidism ~10 years ago, on thyroid medication, currently awaiting blood work and speculating about lowering the medication or 'healing naturally'; prior period of depression that interrupted college; no injuries, chronic pain or movement limitations

signals: Already active and reasonably lean (6'0", 168 lb, sport 5+ days/week) and framed the ask as 'I'm probably classified now... fairly fit. Now it's getting to the next level and leveling up to be athletic'
Professional engineer at GE Aerospace; no price or affordability resistance surfaced (though price was never named)
Self-improvement framing throughout — 'reaching a more actualized version of my full potential'

Caveat against a clean optimizer read: he explicitly deprioritises work ('trying to get good enough at work that I can kind of cruise and get a paycheck'), which is not the successful-operator profile the ICP describes

goals.text: Build strength to move from 'fairly fit' to genuinely athletic — strength he says ping pong, basketball and volleyball cannot give him
Target upper body, shoulders and core as his weakest areas; core specifically to improve coordination and balance for sport
Body recomposition rather than bulk-and-cut phases; would like abs / a six-pack as a milestone
Extend his athletic prime past his late 20s and early 30s — 'I've always loved the concept of having good longevity'
A body he can be 'fully proud of', feeding back into self-love and confidence
Get better at table tennis, including the lower-body base the sport demands
Learn correct kettlebell technique from feedback so he can carry the methodology on himself — 'teaching him how to fish'

pains.text: Cannot establish the habit of strength training; past gym phases produced results but 'it was hard to be consistent'
Getting to the gym itself is the barrier — 'if I could just do it in my apartment, I think that would eliminate... the access issue'
Diet is 'a bit all over the place'; eats out roughly every day and largely one big meal daily; bought pots and pans but never started cooking
Doesn't know what he is doing with weights — depended on a friend to spot him and lost the habit when the friend wasn't there
Is 'all-in on everything' at once (meditation, table tennis, volleyball, basketball, karaoke) and names time as the biggest risk to it all
Sleeping noticeably less than he used to and unsure whether he is off or has a new baseline — 'the only problem is the sleep'
Diagnosed hypothyroidism managed with medication, which he links to the timing of a past depressive episode
Desk-bound engineering work; 'I just get stuck in, like, sitting for, like, long periods of time, and it's actually, like, the worst'

evidence: Discovery ran the full hour with no offer, no price and no close attempt: 'I got a bunch of thoughts for you. Okay. Before we dive into them, though...'
Prospect had a hard stop for a table tennis lesson — 'I actually do have to head out in maybe like 20 minutes'
Rep declined to continue in the car and rebooked: 'why don't we do this? What's your calendar look like tomorrow? I want to find another time to continue the conversation'
Calendar invite sent live for 4pm Eastern the next day; rep initially sent it for the wrong day and corrected it

Counter-evidence on intent being soft: prospect volunteered 'I don't actually think one-on-one would be something that I would do, like, super long-term. It would just be a couple months to get the motions down'
Supporting intent: 'I'm really excited to go all in' and he had already signed up for Primal University two days earlier
outcome.next_step: Continuation call booked for 2026-07-04 4:00pm Eastern (invite sent live); prospect to take it parked in his car with a notebook; Kim or the rep to text a confirmation that morning.

notable.note: The title attributes this call to Andrew Musial but Michael Brideau ran it end to end; the prospect explains he joined through Andrew's Zoom link ('I never actually got an email link to the zoom for this call'). Rep spent 51 minutes in discovery and never reached price, consequence frame or commitment check before the prospect's hard stop — the presentation was pushed wholesale into a second call. Prospect is already a paying/enrolled Primal University member and is being upsold to one-on-one. He discloses medicated hypothyroidism and, unprompted, muses about lowering the medication; the rep engages the mind-body framing rather than deferring to his physician.

quality.notes: Frequent turn-merging rather than wholesale inversion. Rep lines land inside prospect turns (00:01:35 'Does that all work?', 00:13:xx 'What's held you back from doing that so far?', 00:18:20 'Is there anything else that you're doing for exercise currently?', 00:40:xx 'walk me through what... what else are we all in on') and prospect lines land on the rep label (00:07:22 'Height is six foot', 00:42:45 'We're making more, like, we got a promotion at work?'). Role is recoverable from content throughout; no line-level attribution was used for scoring.
